key_impacts: Unprecedented death and devastation with loss of life and property, and disruption of basic services across Uttarakhand.
On 2013-06-17, a raging Mandakini River fueled by incessant rains swept across Kedarnath, killing people including a 16-year-old stable hand.
Families lost breadwinners; children and adolescents were hit hardest, with risks such as discontinuing education due to loss of income.
missing_information: Comprehensive damage and service disruption data

key_impacts: The State Primary School at Farkia was destroyed, reduced to rubble.
For two weeks after the landslide, classes ran from two makeshift locations in the village.
From 13th August onwards, classes moved to dank Panchayat premises that impeded teaching and learning.
Seven months after destruction, there was still no indication of reconstruction.

key_impacts: Families were unable to compensate over time for food shortages and deteriorating health conditions after the floods.
Flood-exposed children did not achieve the usual post-shock catch-up growth and remained shorter than unexposed children from the same neighborhoods.

event_dates: after the tsunami in Sri Lanka
key_impacts: People were displaced to relief camps; nutritional status of children under five, pregnant women and lactating women was assessed.
Malnutrition risk among children of displaced families was highlighted.

event_dates: study of flood-related mortality in Nepal
key_impacts: Children’s flood-related death rate was double that of adults.
Pre-school girls were five times more likely to die than adult men.
